name: scanovich.ai
object_type: Consulting-or-product site — explicitly NOT a portfolio, and included in this set as a contrast/outlier. It is a gated B2B practice site for a one-person document-intelligence consultancy: 'Scanovich is a private document-intelligence practice. A proprietary engine, deployed under NDA inside the client boundary…'. It sells neither software seats nor a résumé; it sells qualification into a scoped engagement. Structurally it inverts almost every portfolio convention — there is no project gallery, no skills list, no CV, no GitHub links, no live demo you can click, and no work history. Where a portfolio says 'here is everything I have built, go look', this site says the opposite: 'the asset is proprietary, deployments are under NDA, access is by introduction'. Its only portfolio-like element is a single first-person founder note. It is best read as the destination-state that a freelance-oriented portfolio evolves toward once the owner stops needing to be evaluated and starts needing to filter.
format_genre: Document — but a very specific and unusual sub-genre: a simulated confidential dossier / legal case file, rendered as a long scroll page. The organising metaphor is total and consistently executed: the page is stamped 'File № SCN-2026-01 · Restricted circulation' in both header-adjacent and footer positions, sections are numbered as legal clauses (§ 01 Position of the practice, § 01a Who should enter, § 02 The asset, § 03 Terms of engagement, § 04 Deployment map), sub-points are decimal-numbered (1.1, 1.2, 1.3 / 3.1, 3.2, 3.3), evidence sections are labelled 'Exhibit A — Cross-border trade' and 'Exhibit B — Marketplace economics', the deep page is a 'Trade deployment dossier' at 'File № SCN-2026-01 / A', the engine diagram is captioned 'Proprietary asset of the practice — annex to the file', the contact form is headed 'Form D-1 · Access request', and the closing statement is 'From the principal of the practice'. It is not a scroll-page in the portfolio sense (no hero → about → projects rhythm) but a paper-file simulation: dark cover, then cream 'vellum' sheets. This is the single most distinctive formal choice in the entire research set.
intent_audience: Gated qualification — the purest example of this mode available. Every CTA is a filter rather than an invitation: 'Request private scoping review', 'Submit a redacted workflow sample', 'Scope a redacted sample', 'A private practice · By introduction and qualification', 'Engagements are few and scoped. Access is by introduction or written request.' The funnel is explicitly stated as three stages — private briefing + async scoping review → scoped paid pilot on redacted samples under NDA → private production deployment inside the client boundary — with the anti-sales promise 'Optional call only after fit is confirmed' and 'This is not a sales form. Every request is read personally, and a scoping review is prepared before any call.' It also states what it refuses, twice: 'It does not sell software seats' and 'Not in scope: generic accelerators, crypto, no-code consultancies, or deck-only AI conversations.' Audience is segmented into four named 'corridors' — principals & family offices, trade/customs/import ops, marketplace operators, legal/contract/compliance — each with its own entry CTA. The addressee is not a recruiter or a peer developer; it is a signatory with personal liability ('where a document, once signed, becomes someone's personal exposure'). Zero job-seeking signal, zero developer-community signal.
seniority_stage: Founder — and the site is engineered so that no other reading is possible. There is no employment history, no title beneath a company, no 'years of experience', no seniority ladder; the owner's only stated role is 'Principal of the practice', a deliberately legal/professional-services term borrowed from law and consulting firms rather than from software. Authority is asserted through accountability rather than tenure: 'I review every brief myself', 'The request is filed directly with the principal of the practice', 'Named practice — direct accountability', 'That standard is mine before it is the system's.' 'Good' for this item therefore means credibility with a liability-bearing buyer — which is why the site optimises for restraint, honest status labels and refusal criteria instead of for breadth of work shown. Note the trade-off this creates for a portfolio-comparison lens: an evaluator cannot verify seniority at all from this site, because there is nothing dated, no employer named, and no artifact to inspect. The founder framing only works because the buyer is expected to arrive pre-warmed by introduction.
language_i18n: English primary with a real Russian surface — the only genuinely bilingual item in the set, and instructive about how to do it. EN is at `/` and is declared canonical both in markup (`rel=canonical` → scanovich.ai/) and in on-page RU copy ('Канонический сайт — на английском'). RU lives at `/ru/`, reached by an 'RU' link in the header (and 'EN' back), with proper `hreflang` alternates for en, ru and x-default, and `inLanguage: ["en","ru"]` in the WebSite JSON-LD. The RU page is not a machine translation of the EN page — it is a shorter, differently-scoped variant: it drops one of the four corridors (3 corridors instead of 4), swaps HS for 'ТН ВЭД' terminology, names Yandex.Market explicitly as the marketplace proof surface where EN keeps it generic, and adds a bridging note ('Эта страница — русская версия досье для квалифицированных заказчиков и продавцов Яндекс.Маркета'). The engagement-terms copy differs by locale too ('not public SaaS tiers on EN'), i.e. the two surfaces are positioned for two different buyer cultures. The header nav labels also localise (Таможня / ВЭД, О Scanovich, Открыть меню). One concrete defect: `/ru/` is served with `<html lang="en">` — the locale is switched in content and metadata but not in the root language attribute, which mis-signals to screen readers and translation tooling. The deep `/customs/` dossier is EN-only, and the RU page links to it with an '(англ.)' honesty marker.
owner_role: Aleksandr Mordvinov — 'Principal of the practice' (also `jobTitle: Founder` in the Person JSON-LD, and `author`/`creator` in the page metadata). No other role, employer, education or work-history claim appears anywhere on the site. The /about/ page is titled 'The principal' with the subtitle 'The name behind the file' and consists of a grayscale/sepia-filtered 128 px portrait plus one paragraph and two lists — it is the shortest 'about' page in the research set. Off-site, the same person maintains a public GitHub profile as `FUYOH666` (display name Aleksandr Mordvinov, bio 'document intelligence for principals & group ops', linking scanovich.ai, LinkedIn in/aleksandr-mordvinov and Telegram ScanovichAI), whose public repos reveal the actual engineering surface the site conceals: `Scanovich.ai-audio-call` (local-first call analytics, FastAPI + faster-whisper + vLLM + Telegram bot), `Services-BGE` (BGE-M3 embedding and reranker microservices for Qdrant hybrid search), `VoiceToText` (local Whisper/MLX on Apple Silicon), `LocalScript`, `attestrwa`, and `scanovich-webUI` (Open WebUI + LiteLLM orchestration). None of these are linked from scanovich.ai.
sections_present:
Mapped against the portfolio checklist, most sections are absent by design.

PRESENT (homepage, EN): hero ('Private document intelligence for files that carry liability'), a three-line value triad (messy documents → structured review / recommendations → source-backed explanations / human sign-off → audit trail), 'What it does', an inline 'Illustrative output' specimen card, § 01 Position of the practice (1.1–1.3), § 01a Who should enter (four audience corridors), § 02 The asset (a 5-stage pipeline diagram: Ingest → Normalize → Classify → Explain → Sign-off), § 03 Terms of engagement (3.1 briefing/scoping, 3.2 scoped paid pilot, 3.3 private production deployment), § 04 Deployment map (six surfaces with honest status labels: Live / Live / Scoped pilot / By introduction ×3), Exhibit A (cross-border trade), Exhibit B (marketplace economics), a signed first-person note 'From the principal of the practice', a gated contact form ('Form D-1 · Access request'), and a minimal footer (monogram, file number, © 2026 Scanovich).

ADDITIONAL ROUTES: `/customs/` — a long vertical case-study/dossier for the trade vertical (the exposure narrative, an annotated illustrative output, a measured-workflow metrics block, six numbered capabilities with Live/Pilot/Roadmap labels, four buyer personas, four 'terms before engagement' boundary statements, and an FAQ). `/about/` — 'The principal'. `/ru/` — the Russian variant.

ABSENT: About (in the personal sense — one paragraph total, no bio, no story, no interests), Projects/portfolio gallery (no client work shown, no logos, no case names — the only 'work' shown is a synthetic specimen), Experience (no employment history at all), Skills (no technology list; the stack is never named), Resume/CV (none, in any format), Blog/Writing (none), testimonials, pricing, team page. Notably also absent: any GitHub link, despite the owner having a public GitHub with directly relevant repos.
nav_pattern: Multi-page (4 routes: /, /customs/, /about/, /ru/) with each route itself a long single-column scroll. The header is a slim sticky bar (`bg-canvas/90`, hairline `border-white/[0.06]`) carrying a wordmark rendered as 'scanovich' + a muted '.' + a muted 'ai', then — at ≥sm — text links (Таможня/Customs, About, RU/EN) and one filled champagne CTA button 'Request private scoping review'; below sm the links collapse behind a hamburger with correct `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls="home-nav-mobile"` and an `sr-only` label. There are no in-page jump links and no section index despite the page being ~9 numbered sections long — navigation within a page is pure scroll, which is the one clear usability regression versus a portfolio's sticky rail. Instead of jump links the site repeats the same conversion target: the string 'Request private scoping review' (or a corridor-specific variant like 'Scope a redacted sample' / 'Submit a redacted workflow sample') appears roughly eight times down the homepage, all pointing at `#contact`. Cross-route links are contextual and prose-embedded ('Trade operators: full deployment dossier at scanovich.ai/customs/', 'See § 04 deployment map on the dossier cover'), and one CTA carries an intent parameter — `/#contact?intent=sample` — which the contact component reads via `useSearchParams`, auto-scrolls to the form and swaps in sample-specific placeholder copy plus a hidden `_intent=sample` field.
visual_style: A 'confidential dossier' aesthetic — restrained, editorial, print-derived, and deliberately outside every current web-design trend. There is no bento grid, no neo-brutalism, no glassmorphism, no kinetic typography, no gradient mesh, no 3D, and no illustration; the only image on the entire homepage is absent (the sole `` in the site is the owner's portrait, on /about/). Design-trend alignment is best described as anti-trend luxury/legal-services: it reads closer to a private bank's annual report or a law firm's engagement letter than to a tech landing page. The execution rests on a two-surface contrast: a near-black 'canvas' cover (#070708) for the hero and header, then cream 'vellum' paper sheets (#EFE9DB, #F6F1E6) for the dossier body — literally simulating a dark folder opening onto printed pages. On top of that: a film-grain overlay applied via `body::after` using an inline SVG `feTurbulence fractalNoise` at 2.5% opacity with `mix-blend-mode: overlay` (paper tooth); a `.letterpress` utility on the h1 (`text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.05), 0 -1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.75)`) to emboss the headline; hairline 1px rules and `rounded-sm`/`rounded-[1px]` corners throughout (no soft cards); an 'S' monogram seal used as a section divider and in the footer; mono micro-caps with wide letter-spacing (`font-mono text-[10px] uppercase tracking-[0.2em]`) for eyebrows, clause numbers and status labels; and status chips (Live / Scoped pilot / By introduction / Roadmap) as the main structural motif of the deployment map. The owner's portrait is filtered `grayscale-[35%] sepia-[15%]` with a 1px radius — an archival-photograph treatment consistent with the file metaphor. Residual evidence in the CSS/JS of an earlier, more conventional dark-SaaS skin (emerald/brand accents, `bg-surface-1`, `#1e2028` borders) survives as a second unused 'variant' alongside the shipped 'private' variant — i.e. the dossier art direction is a deliberate repositioning away from a standard AI-startup look [uncertain].
color_typography: Fixed art direction, no light/dark toggle and no `prefers-color-scheme` handling anywhere in the CSS — because the page already contains both a dark and a light surface by design. Tokens (from `:root` and the Tailwind theme): canvas #070708 (near-black cover) with `bg-elevated` #0F0F11 and `bg-card` #141416; canvas-warm #F5F4F0 for text on dark, canvas-muted #8A8880; vellum #EFE9DB and vellum-sheet #F6F1E6 (cream paper), vellum-ink #211D17 (warm near-black type on cream), vellum-muted #6F6555; champagne #C4B5A0 as the primary accent (CTA fill, hairlines, eyebrows, focus rings at `/50` and `/15`), champagne-hover #D4C9B8; seal #A6813F, a brass/gold used for links and CTAs on the cream surface; and a single semantic token `--proof-trade: #6B7F6E` (muted green) for the trade proof surface. Borders are almost all `hsla(0,0%,100%,.06)` — a 6% white hairline. Typography is a three-family system, all self-hosted via `next/font` (7 preloaded .woff2, zero runtime font requests despite `preconnect` hints to Google Fonts remaining in the head): Instrument Serif as `--font-display` for every heading (`font-display` on h1/h2/h3, `Georgia, serif` fallback), Playfair Display also bundled as a display face, and Inter as `--font-main`/`--font-sans` for body, with a `ui-monospace` stack for micro-caps and the specimen card's numeric/code content. Headings are fluid-sized with `clamp()` (h1 `clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 3.5rem)`, h2 `clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 2.75rem)`) at `leading-[1.12] tracking-tight`. The serif-display + mono-micro-caps + cream-paper combination is what produces the legal-document register.
motion: Restrained, scroll-triggered, and correctly gated. Framer Motion is bundled and used in the `whileInView` + `viewport` pattern (with `initial`/`animate` pairs) — i.e. sections and clause blocks fade/rise in once as they enter the viewport, matching the 'turning pages of a file' idea. Beyond that there is only CSS: `transition-colors` / `transition-all` on links and buttons, hover elevation on the CTA (`hover:shadow-glow`), and `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `<html>`. No parallax, no scroll-jacking, no counters, no autoplay media, no cursor effects, no loading animation. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` IS respected and does two specific things: it resets `scroll-behavior` to `auto` and it disables the `body::after` film-grain overlay entirely (`display: none`) — a thoughtful touch, since an animated-looking noise texture is exactly the sort of thing motion-sensitive users report as uncomfortable. Caveat: the reduce block does not appear to neutralise the Framer Motion entrance transforms themselves, so a reduced-motion visitor may still get the in-view reveals unless Framer's own `useReducedMotion` is wired up in the components [uncertain].
responsiveness_mobile: Fully responsive and, because the format_genre is a document rather than an interactive gimmick, it degrades essentially perfectly — there is nothing to degrade. Concretely: all display type is fluid via `clamp()` so headlines never need breakpoint overrides; the header collapses from a text-link row to a hamburger at `sm` with an ARIA-wired disclosure panel (`hidden sm:flex` on the link row, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` on the toggle) and the nav items become full-width tap targets (`py-2 ... sm:py-0`); the audience-corridor grid and the FAQ/persona grids stack; the contact form is a single column at all sizes with two fields pairing up on wider viewports; the owner portrait steps `h-28 w-28` → `sm:h-32 sm:w-32`; the pipeline diagram (Ingest → Normalize → Classify → Explain → Sign-off) is built from text nodes and '→' glyphs rather than an SVG or canvas, so it reflows instead of overflowing — a notably robust choice for the one diagram on the page. The specimen 'Illustrative output' card is the densest element (numbered rows, HS code, confidence, GRI trace, sources) and is the most likely candidate for cramped rendering on a narrow phone [uncertain]. Two genuine mobile costs: (1) there are no in-page jump links on any viewport, so a phone user must scroll the full ~9-section homepage or the much longer /customs/ dossier linearly, with no section index and no back-to-top; (2) the CTA is repeated ~8 times down the page, which reads as reassuring rhythm on desktop but as insistent on a phone. Content is fully server-rendered, so a slow or JS-disabled mobile client still gets the entire document — only the contact form (a client component) is missing without JS.
framework_hosting: Next.js 14.2.33 on the App Router (`app/layout` + `app/page` chunks, `main-app`, RSC flight payload embedded in the document, React Server Components with a small set of client components including `ContactSectionClient`), Tailwind CSS with a bespoke design-token theme (canvas/vellum/champagne/seal), Framer Motion for scroll reveals, `next/font` for self-hosted Instrument Serif + Playfair Display + Inter, `next/image` for the single portrait, and Lucide-style inline SVG icons. Rendering is server-side/ISR rather than static export — the origin returns `cache-control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300`, so pages are revalidated on a 5-minute edge window. Hosting: Render.com (the response carries Render's `rndr-id` header) behind Cloudflare (`cf-ray`, `cf-cache-status`, `alt-svc: h3`), with `x-content-type-options: nosniff` set. Forms are handled by a third-party endpoint (Formspree, `https://formspree.io/f/mojkkgnp`, plain POST) rather than a Next API route — so there is no backend of the owner's own exposed by the site. Domain signal: a bare brand name on the `.ai` TLD — a deliberate category-signalling choice (AI practice) rather than the personal-name `.com` a portfolio would pick; the `.ai` here is doing positioning work, and pairs with a `/customs/` path used as a vertical landing surface. SEO/AI-crawler infrastructure is unusually deliberate for a site this small: `sitemap.xml` with per-route `lastmod`/`changefreq`/`priority` (/, /customs/ at 0.95, /ru/ at 0.8, /about/ at 0.7), correct `hreflang` triples, canonical tags, five distinct JSON-LD blocks (Organization, Person, WebSite, and two Service entries — 'Private document intelligence' and 'Cross-border trade document intelligence'), an extensive `keywords` meta (a legacy tactic), and a `robots.txt` that takes an explicit position on AI: `GPTBot: Disallow` and `Google-Extended: Disallow` (no training) while `OAI-SearchBot: Allow` and `ChatGPT-User: Allow` (yes retrieval/citation) — i.e. opt out of model training, opt in to being surfaced in AI search. It also sets `format-detection: telephone=no, address=no, email=no`.
performance_a11y: Performance: light and fast, with a slightly heavier JS budget than a static portfolio because of the App Router + Framer Motion baseline. Homepage document 119.9 KB raw / ~15.5 KB over the wire (a large document for the content, because the RSC flight payload is inlined twice-over in the markup); CSS 42.3 KB raw / 8.3 KB compressed; JS ~830 KB raw across 11 chunks but ~236 KB compressed (the three biggest being 70.9 KB, 54.4 KB and 50.6 KB compressed — React + App Router runtime + Framer Motion), plus a `nomodule` polyfill chunk. Seven preloaded self-hosted woff2 font files; exactly one image site-wide (the 128 px portrait, `loading="lazy"`, via next/image). Third-party requests: Google Analytics 4 and Yandex Metrica, plus Formspree only on submit — no CDN scripts, no embeds, no external fonts at runtime. Fully server-rendered content behind Cloudflare with a 5-minute edge cache, so first paint should be quick and the copy is fully crawlable. Accessibility: decent-but-not-exemplary — clearly better than a typical marketing site, clearly behind an accessibility-specialist portfolio. Positives: sensible heading order (one `<h1>` per page, `<h2>` per numbered section, `<h3>` per card) with no skipped levels; `focus-visible:ring-1 ring-champagne/50` applied consistently to nav links, CTAs and form inputs, so keyboard traversal is visible everywhere; the mobile nav toggle is a real disclosure (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `sr-only` label); 31 `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative SVGs; two meaningful `aria-label`s on the non-text content that needs them ('Illustrative classification output', 'Engine pipeline from ingest to human sign-off'); every form field has an explicit `<label htmlFor>` bound to a real `id`; `prefers-reduced-motion` handled; contrast is strong on both surfaces (#211D17 on #EFE9DB and #F5F4F0 on #070708 are both far above AA). Gaps: NO skip-to-content link anywhere; `<html lang="en">` is hard-coded even on the Russian page, so RU content is announced with an English voice; no `<main>` landmark labelling beyond the element itself and no other landmark `aria-label`s; the contact form is a client-only component, so with JS disabled the sole conversion path silently disappears (the section renders `null`); the brass `seal` (#A6813F) on cream is the one colour pair worth measuring, and small mono micro-caps at `text-[10px]` with `tracking-[0.2em]` are legible but near the practical floor.
analytics_instrumentation: Dual-stack and geographically deliberate: Google Analytics 4 (`gtag/js?id=G-YQFTKVM3L2`) plus Yandex Metrica (preconnect to `mc.yandex.ru`, counter loaded client-side) — the latter chosen because the RU surface and the Yandex.Market marketplace vertical are a real part of the funnel. No Plausible, Umami, Fathom, Vercel Analytics, PostHog or session replay. There is additionally custom conversion instrumentation the other items in this set lack: the contact form fires a one-shot analytics event on first field focus (guarded by a ref so it cannot double-fire), i.e. form-start is tracked separately from form-submit, and the form carries hidden `_locale` and `_intent` fields so submissions are attributable to language surface and to which CTA produced them. No cookie or consent banner is presented despite two trackers and an EU-facing audience.
project_presentation:
This is where the contrast with a portfolio is sharpest: there are no projects shown, and the absence is the strategy. No client names, no logos, no case-study links, no screenshots of real work, no repositories, and no live demo of any kind — no Vercel app, no HF Space, no sandbox, not even a gated video. The stated reason is repeated across the site: 'It does not sell software seats. The proprietary engine is deployed privately, under NDA, inside the client's boundary'; 'Proprietary IP — available under license and NDA after qualification'; 'SKU-level unit economics deployed under NDA — proof on the same engine, not a public self-serve layer on this site'; 'Qualified walkthrough on redacted samples after access request.' Live-demo availability is therefore 0%, by policy rather than by neglect.

In place of a project gallery there are four substitute proof devices, and they are the borrowable part:

1. A SYNTHETIC SPECIMEN, labelled as such. An 'Illustrative output — review-ready classification' card, present on the homepage and expanded on /customs/: input string '"LED desk lamp, 10W, USB-C, touch dimmer"' → numbered output rows — (1) HS / TN VED `9405 42 390 0`, (2) Confidence `0.86`, (3) GRI trace 'Rule 1 → Heading 9405 (lamps and lighting fittings); Rule 6 → Subheading 9405.42 (LED, electric)', plus Certification 'EAEU TR 004/2011: mandatory declaration of conformity' and Sources '· EAEU TN VED, Chapter 94 · TR CU 004/2011, Annex 1'. It is fabricated, it says so in its own label, and it still demonstrates output shape, reasoning trace, confidence and citation discipline better than a screenshot of a dashboard would. The word 'Illustrative' does the ethical work.

2. A DEPLOYMENT MAP WITH HONEST STATUS LABELS (§ 04) — six surfaces, each explicitly staged: Live (cross-border trade HS/TN VED), Live (marketplace unit economics), Scoped pilot (declaration archive search), By introduction (general counsel / contract corpus), By introduction (permitting / subsurface dossiers), By introduction (multi-entity group operations). Repeated on /customs/ at capability granularity: capabilities 01–04 marked Live, 05 marked Pilot, 06 ('Declaration draft under R.055') marked Roadmap with the caveat 'A controlled next step, not a promise.' The section headline is literally 'One engine. Honest labels on every surface', and /customs/ states 'Honest about what is live — anything in roadmap is labelled that way. No fake "already GA" on features still under co-development.' A pre-emptive, itemised anti-vaporware disclosure is rare and is the strongest trust device on the site.

3. A PROCESS DIAGRAM AS THE ARTEFACT (§ 02 'The asset') — Ingest (messy inputs) → Normalize (extract · schema) → Classify (explainable codes) → Explain (sources · trace) → Sign-off (human gate), captioned 'Proprietary asset of the practice — annex to the file', with the accompanying claim that vertical products are 'wedges and proof on the same architecture — not separate experiments'. The architecture, not the output, is positioned as the thing being sold.

4. BUYER-PERSONA MIRRORS instead of project cards — /customs/ substitutes 'Who this is for' (importer ops lead, customs broker, trade compliance manager, platform/software vendor), each written as a pain narrative the reader can self-identify with, and the homepage's § 01a does the same with four 'corridors'. The reader recognises themselves where they would otherwise be evaluating someone else's work.

The cost of all this is real and worth stating plainly for the research set: a cold visitor cannot verify that the engine exists. There is no artefact, no third-party attestation, no named reference, and the owner's actually-public and relevant GitHub repos are not linked. The design assumes a warm introduction is doing the verification off-site.
resume_integration_mode: None of the four modes — there is no CV in any form. No PDF download, no inline work history, no dates, no education, nothing ATS-parseable, and no 'Experience' section to parse. The functional substitutes are (a) the /about/ page, whose entire body is one paragraph plus two bulleted lists ('Deployed — live surfaces, honest labels' and 'Terms of engagement — who should request access'), i.e. a capability statement rather than a biography, and (b) a LinkedIn link (in/aleksandr-mordvinov) which is the only machine-readable career record and appears exactly once, in /about/'s footer area and inside the JSON-LD `sameAs`. Structured data compensates slightly: the Person entity declares `jobTitle: Founder` and a `knowsAbout` array (HS Classification, TN VED, Customs Workflows, EAEU Technical Regulations, Supplier Spreadsheet Normalization, Marketplace Profitability Analytics, Enterprise AI Systems) — effectively a skills list that exists only for machines and is invisible to human readers. This is the intended inversion: a résumé invites evaluation, and this site is built to refuse evaluation until after qualification.
proof_verifiability:
Weak in the conventional sense, and unusually honest about being weak — the site's proof strategy is to be scrupulous about labelling unverifiable things rather than to make them verifiable.

WHAT IS NOT VERIFIABLE (i.e. essentially everything material): no client is named, no logo is shown, no case study, no testimonial, no reference, no third-party attestation, no audit, no certification, no press coverage, no award, and no public artefact. A web search for the practice and the principal surfaces no independent coverage at all. The 'Live' status of two deployment surfaces is an unbacked assertion. 'Deployed under NDA' is simultaneously the value proposition and an unfalsifiable claim, and the site never offers an escrowed alternative (no anonymised client quote, no 'verified by' third party, no redacted engagement letter).

WHAT IS DONE WELL: every claim is scoped and labelled at the point of assertion. The specimen output is marked 'Illustrative'. The metrics block is marked 'Measured workflow · interim' and 'Golden-set benchmark (internal, 45 cases)' with the explicit disclaimer 'Illustrative workflow metrics on an internal golden set… not a guarantee on live declarations' and 'Interim dev LLM; production deployment metrics provided per engagement.' Every capability carries Live / Pilot / Roadmap. Boundaries are stated before scope ('Not a replacement for a broker', 'Final responsibility stays with the qualified specialist', 'No fake "already GA"'). The regulatory references are the one genuinely checkable thing on the site — EAEU TN VED Chapter 94, TR CU 004/2011 Annex 1, TR 020, TR 025, GRI Rules 1 and 6, 'R.055' — a domain reader can confirm these are cited correctly, which functions as a competence proof even without an artefact.

THE UNFORCED ERROR: the owner has a public GitHub (`FUYOH666`) containing directly corroborating engineering work — a Scanovich-branded local-first analytics platform, BGE-M3/Qdrant hybrid-search microservices, an Open WebUI + LiteLLM orchestration repo — and the site links to none of it. Verifiable technical evidence exists one hop away and is deliberately or carelessly left unlinked; a single 'engineering notes' link would materially raise the floor without breaching any NDA.
quantified_impact:
Present, narrow, and caveated to an unusual degree — which makes it a useful counter-example to both the metric-free portfolio and the metric-inflating one. The numbers, all on /customs/ under the heading 'Measured workflow · interim': 91% heading accuracy at the 4-digit HS/TN VED level; a median 14 seconds per line; an internal golden set of 45 cases; operator-in-the-loop throughout. Each figure comes with its own definitional footnote — heading accuracy is defined as 'share of golden-set lines where the model's 4-digit HS/TN VED heading matches the reference label after GRI trace review'; the golden set is broken down into three tiers (easy/clean supplier rows, adversarial/ambiguous descriptions and mixed languages, practice-style/realistic noise); latency is attributed to 'the interim dev stack' with 'production deployments are sized per engagement'. The specimen card additionally shows a per-row confidence score (0.86). And crucially, the site declines to quote an ROI number, saying instead: 'Paid pilots agree KPIs on redacted samples under NDA — typically heading agreement, review time, and certification flag precision — not fixed ROI percentages', plus 'Client pilots are measured separately on redacted data under NDA.'

Assessment: n=45 on an internally-constructed set with an interim model is a weak benchmark by any research standard, and there is no baseline comparison, no confusion analysis and no external replication — but the site presents it as exactly that weak, names its size, discloses the tiering, and refuses to extrapolate. That is a materially more credible posture than either a portfolio with no numbers at all or one claiming '99% accuracy' with no denominator. There are no business metrics anywhere (no users, revenue, clients served, documents processed, or cost saved), which is consistent with the confidentiality frame but leaves the practice's actual scale entirely unknown.
content_freshness: Very fresh, and freshness is instrumented rather than merely claimed. The homepage was served with `Last-Modified: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 01:22:40` — one day before this research — and `sitemap.xml` carries matching per-route `lastmod` timestamps of `2026-07-29T01:22:33Z` for all four routes with `changefreq: weekly` on the two commercial pages. The file number itself is a dated device: 'File № SCN-2026-01' and '© 2026 Scanovich', so the current year is visible on every screen (with the corresponding maintenance obligation each January). The § 04 deployment map and the /customs/ capability list act as a de-facto status board — Live / Scoped pilot / By introduction / Roadmap labels are exactly the sort of thing that reads as current, and 'Today EAEU TN VED' plus 'the first users are' phrasing signal an evolving state. There is no dated changelog, no /now page, no blog, and no 'currently working on' widget, so recency is inferred from HTTP metadata and status labels rather than stated. One thing that would go stale invisibly: nothing on the page carries its own last-reviewed date, so a 'Live' label could persist long after the fact without any visitor-detectable signal.
writing_tone: The most distinctive voice in the research set: austere, declarative, legalistic, and consistently subtractive. Sentences are short and often verbless-by-design fragments used as headings ('Four corridors. One practice — pick the file that matches your office.'; 'Boundaries stated before scope.'; 'One engine. Honest labels on every surface.'; 'The name behind the file.'). The register is professional-services/private-banking rather than software — 'practice', 'principal', 'engagement', 'corridor', 'exhibit', 'annex', 'restricted circulation', 'by introduction' — and the em dash is the signature punctuation mark. It is a tone built out of refusal: much of the copy states what the practice will not do ('It does not sell software seats'; 'This is not a sales form'; 'not generative counsel'; 'Not a replacement for a broker'; 'Not in scope: generic accelerators, crypto, no-code consultancies, or deck-only AI conversations'; 'Optional call only after fit is confirmed'). Zero exclamation marks, zero emoji, no humour, no easter eggs, no first-person warmth anywhere except one deliberate passage — the signed closing note, which is the only place the voice becomes human: 'Every output this engine produces was designed to survive one test: a person with authority signs it, and stands behind it. That standard is mine before it is the system's. If your office runs documents that carry that weight, request access — I review every brief myself. — A. Mordvinov, Principal of the practice.' The scarcity of that one first-person moment is what gives it force. Risks of the register: it can read as pretentious or as LARPing institutional authority that a one-person practice has not yet earned, and the density of gatekeeping language ('qualification', 'restricted circulation', 'by introduction') will repel as many readers as it filters — which is the stated intent, but it is a bet.
standout_features:
Ranked by how borrowable each is for a conventional SE/hackathon portfolio.

CHEAP AND GENUINELY WORTH STEALING:
1. HONEST STATUS LABELS ON EVERY SURFACE. A fixed vocabulary — Live / Scoped pilot / By introduction / Roadmap — applied to every capability and vertical, with the explicit promise 'No fake "already GA" on features still under co-development' and 'A controlled next step, not a promise.' A portfolio can adopt this verbatim for its project grid (Shipped / In progress / Prototype / Archived / Idea) and it instantly solves the credibility problem of the half-finished side project. This is the single most transferable idea on the site.
2. THE LABELLED SYNTHETIC SPECIMEN. When you cannot show real work (NDA, internal tooling, private client data), build one fabricated end-to-end output and label it 'Illustrative'. Scanovich's version shows an input string, a structured result, a confidence score, a rule-by-rule reasoning trace and cited sources — it communicates output shape and rigour better than a dashboard screenshot, and the honest label costs nothing. Directly applicable to any engineer whose best work is behind a corporate firewall.
3. METRICS WITH THEIR DENOMINATOR AND THEIR CAVEAT ATTACHED. '91% heading accuracy (4-digit) · median 14s per line' is immediately followed by the definition of the metric, the size and composition of the evaluation set (45 cases across easy/adversarial/practice tiers), and the disclaimer that it is an interim dev stack and not a guarantee. Weak numbers presented this transparently read stronger than strong numbers presented bare.
4. STATE WHAT YOU REFUSE. 'Not in scope: generic accelerators, crypto, no-code consultancies, or deck-only AI conversations.' A short exclusion list is the cheapest possible authority signal and doubles as inbound filtering.
5. ONE SIGNED FIRST-PERSON PARAGRAPH, placed last, in a site that is otherwise impersonal. The contrast is what makes it land. A portfolio drowning in first-person copy gets nothing from this; a terse one gets a lot.
6. INTENT-CARRYING CTAs. `/#contact?intent=sample` auto-scrolls to the form, swaps the placeholder copy to sample-specific prompts, and writes a hidden `_intent` field so the submission arrives pre-labelled with which CTA produced it. About twenty lines of code and it makes a single form behave like several.
7. FORM-START ANALYTICS. A one-shot event fired on first field focus (ref-guarded against double-firing), separate from submit — so abandonment is measurable, not invisible. Almost no portfolio does this.
8. AN OPINIONATED `robots.txt` FOR THE AI ERA. `GPTBot: Disallow` and `Google-Extended: Disallow` (no training) alongside `OAI-SearchBot: Allow` and `ChatGPT-User: Allow` (yes retrieval). Four lines, and it is a real 2026-relevant stance rather than a default.
9. SET EXPECTATIONS INSIDE THE FORM. 'This is not a sales form. Every request is read personally, and a scoping review is prepared before any call — expect a reply within one business day', followed by a numbered 'What happens after you submit'. Raises completion rates and pre-empts the ghosting anxiety every contact form creates.
10. THE FLUID-TEXT DIAGRAM. The five-stage pipeline is built from text nodes and '→' glyphs rather than an SVG or canvas, so it reflows on mobile instead of overflowing, and it stays selectable, translatable and crawlable. A better default than exporting a diagram from Figma.
11. REDUCED-MOTION THAT ALSO KILLS THE TEXTURE. `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the film-grain overlay, not just transitions — an unusually considerate reading of the media query.

MODERATE EFFORT, HIGH DIFFERENTIATION:
12. THE DOSSIER METAPHOR CARRIED ALL THE WAY DOWN. File number, restricted-circulation stamp, § clause numbering, decimal sub-clauses, Exhibit A/B, 'annex to the file', 'Form D-1 · Access request', an 'S' monogram seal as divider. The lesson is not 'do legal documents' — it is that a single organising metaphor applied to naming, numbering, colour and typography simultaneously produces more perceived design quality than any amount of individual visual polish.
13. THE TWO-SURFACE COLOUR STRATEGY: near-black cover → cream vellum body, with grain and letterpress. It gets the visual interest a dark-mode-only portfolio lacks without needing a theme toggle, illustration or 3D.
14. A LOCALISED VARIANT THAT IS ACTUALLY DIFFERENT. The RU page is not a translation: different corridor count, different terminology (ТН ВЭД), a named local marketplace (Yandex.Market), a different commercial frame, and an explicit note that EN is canonical — plus correct hreflang and a locale-tagged form submission. If a bilingual portfolio is on the table, this is how to scope the second language.
15. AUDIENCE CORRIDORS INSTEAD OF A CAPABILITIES LIST. Four self-identification blocks each with their own CTA, so the reader routes themselves. The portfolio analogue is segmenting by 'hiring for X / hiring for Y / want to collaborate'.

WHAT NOT TO COPY:
16. The total absence of inspectable artefacts. This only works with a warm introduction doing the verification off-site; a job-seeking engineer who hides everything has no funnel left. And the site commits the specific error of not linking the owner's own public, directly relevant GitHub repositories — verifiable evidence sitting one hop away, unused.
17. Zero in-page navigation across a nine-section homepage and a much longer dossier page.
18. The institutional-authority register at one-person scale. 'Restricted circulation' on a public website is a bet that can read as either discipline or theatre, and it has no upside for a junior or mid-level engineer.

THE STRUCTURAL LESSON FOR THIS RESEARCH SET: this is the ROI mirror-image of a portfolio. A portfolio maximises inspectable surface area to earn an evaluation; this site minimises it to force a qualification. Both are coherent, and which is correct is a pure function of whether the owner has a warm-introduction pipeline. The transferable core is narrower and more valuable than the aesthetic: label the maturity of everything you show, attach the denominator to every number, say what you refuse, and give your one fabricated example an honest name.
originality_vs_template: Fully custom, no identifiable template lineage. This is not a Next.js starter or a bought landing-page theme: the design tokens (canvas/vellum/champagne/seal/proof-trade), the SVG feTurbulence grain overlay, the `.letterpress` text-shadow utility, the § clause numbering system, the Exhibit structure, the 'Form D-1' framing, the corridor blocks and the locale-variant architecture are all bespoke, and the copy is unmistakably written rather than assembled. It resembles nothing in the portfolio-template ecosystem and nothing in the standard AI-startup landing-page genre (no gradient hero, no logo cloud, no pricing table, no feature triptych). One archaeological caveat worth recording: the shipped bundle still contains a second, unused visual variant using emerald/brand accents, `bg-surface-1` and `#1e2028` borders — the residue of a more conventional dark-SaaS skin that the current 'private/vellum' variant replaced, alongside a `variant` prop that selects between them. So the dossier art direction appears to be a deliberate repositioning away from a generic AI-product look rather than the first idea [uncertain].
source_available: No. The site's own source is not public — there is no scanovich.ai repository, and no source link, GitHub icon or engineering-notes page appears anywhere on any route. This is consistent with the stated posture ('Proprietary asset of the practice', 'available under license and NDA after qualification'), so it is a policy rather than an omission. But the dogfooding signal is being left on the table: the owner maintains a public GitHub account (`FUYOH666`, display name Aleksandr Mordvinov, bio 'document intelligence for principals & group ops', website scanovich.ai) whose repos are directly relevant and reasonably substantial — `Scanovich.ai-audio-call` (local-first call analytics: FastAPI, faster-whisper, vLLM, Telegram bot, on-prem deployment paths; also mirrored under a second account), `Services-BGE` (BGE-M3 embedding + BGE-Reranker-v2-m3 microservices for Qdrant hybrid search), `scanovich-webUI` (Open WebUI + LiteLLM orchestration), `VoiceToText` (local Whisper/MLX), `LocalScript`, `attestrwa`. None of these are linked from the site, and they carry no stars or external validation. Net: closed source by design, with adjacent public engineering evidence that exists but is deliberately or carelessly disconnected from the commercial surface — the clearest missed opportunity on the site.
contact_methods: A single deliberately narrow funnel, plus two named side channels. PRIMARY: the gated form, headed 'Form D-1 · Access request' / 'Request a private scoping review', posting to Formspree (`https://formspree.io/f/mojkkgnp`). Four required fields with explicit labels and revealing placeholder copy — Name ('How should we address you?'), Email, Capacity/office ('Redacted workflow sample · e.g. import ops, compliance lead, counsel'), and a 4-row Note ('The document workflow you need scoped — entities, jurisdictions, who signs' / for the sample intent: 'Redacted workflow sample — document type, volume, who signs, jurisdictions involved') — note that the form asks for the reader's authority and their signatory chain, i.e. it is a qualification instrument, not a message box. Hidden `_locale` and `_intent` fields tag the submission. Around the form: 'This is not a sales form. Every request is read personally, and a scoping review is prepared before any call — expect a reply within one business day'; a numbered 'What happens after you submit' ('A scoping review is prepared — no calls, no sales sequence' / 'You receive a written reply within one business day'); 'The request is filed directly with the principal of the practice'; and a stated timezone/SLA ('JST (UTC+9). Email — within one business day') — which incidentally discloses that the practice operates on Japan time. SECONDARY: a 'Direct line' Telegram link (t.me/ScanovichAI), a 'Book a briefing slot' mailto, and `private@scanovich.ai` rendered as a link. TERTIARY: LinkedIn (in/aleksandr-mordvinov), appearing once on /about/ and in JSON-LD `sameAs`. Placement: the CTA is repeated ~8 times down the homepage (header button, hero pair, each of the four corridors, Exhibit B, the signed note) all resolving to the same `#contact` anchor — high-frequency, single-destination, no alternative path. Notably absent: no phone, no calendar/Calendly/Cal.com embed (a call is explicitly withheld until after qualification), no GitHub, no X/Twitter, no Discord, no newsletter. Fragility worth flagging: the contact section is a client-only React component that renders `null` without JavaScript, so the site's sole conversion path vanishes for a JS-disabled or script-blocked visitor.
pii_exposure: Low and well-managed on the owner's side; a couple of second-order notes. Deliberately public: real name (Aleksandr Mordvinov, in visible copy, `<meta name="author">`, `creator`, and two JSON-LD entities), one portrait photograph on /about/ (filtered grayscale/sepia, 128 px), a role-scoped email `private@scanovich.ai` (a functional alias, not a personal Gmail — a better choice than most items in this set), a Telegram handle (t.me/ScanovichAI, branded rather than personal), and a LinkedIn profile URL. No phone number, no postal address, no personal/consumer email, no employer-internal detail, no family or location detail. The site even sets `format-detection: telephone=no, address=no, email=no` to stop mobile browsers auto-linkifying anything. Two incidental disclosures worth noting: the contact copy states 'JST (UTC+9)', which pins the principal's operating timezone (and by inference likely residence) more precisely than any other content on the site; and the off-site GitHub profile the site does not link nonetheless connects the professional identity to a personal handle (`FUYOH666`) and an Instagram account, so the separation between practice and person is only one search away. Visitor-side privacy is the weaker half: Google Analytics 4 and Yandex Metrica both run with no cookie or consent banner on an EU-and-RU-facing site, and the contact form ships visitor-submitted business-sensitive detail (workflow description, jurisdictions, who signs, organisational capacity) through a third-party US form processor (Formspree) — a slight tension with a practice whose entire pitch is data-boundary discipline and NDA-first handling, and one that a short privacy note beside the form would resolve.
